svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: CareLoop architecture: three trust zones, one policy engine, an independent read-back
svg.desc: An inbound email and its PDF attachments enter as UNTRUSTED data, together with the output of the two LLM agents. Eight deterministic graph nodes, all TRUSTED application code, drive the case. One policy engine reading one rules.yaml decides at three call sites: the gate node, the Strands BeforeToolCall hook, and the gated tool wrapper. Validated facts live in the CONTROLLED zone. Two effects reach real providers: the booking goes over HTTP to Demo World, a separate process, and upload_document crosses into Amazon S3. Verification re-reads each provider on its own separate request, never the effect's own response.
svg.text: CareLoop
trust zones, the authority gate, and the independent read-back
The model proposes. Deterministic code authorises. A separate read of an external system confirms what happened.

g.text: one of exactly two model-backed stages; neither holds authority

svg.text: UNTRUSTED
what the world sends, and what the models say

g.text: as data, never as a rule

svg.text: A model's output lands in the same
zone as an attacker's document:
typed, read, and gated like any
other input.
TRUSTED
denied: replan, told a ReasonCode and nothing else
GraphBuilder · every node subclasses MultiAgentBase · bounds from set_max_node_executions, set_execution_timeout, set_node_timeout
Caregiver
approve or reject.
Releases one exact
call. Mints no fact.
PolicyEngine
one engine, one rules.yaml, three call sites
ALLOW · DENY · REQUIRE_HUMAN, deterministic, deny by default
rules are declarative in rules.yaml, never encoded in Python
argument classes belong to the tool registry: DESTINATION, AUTHORITY, VALUE
what the model is told back: a closed ReasonCode, never interpolated
BeforeToolCallEvent.cancel_tool
@gated_tool wrapper (backstop)
Two enforcement sites at the tool boundary, backed by the
same deterministic PolicyGate decision — not two engines.
Each is proven sufficient alone; with neither, the attack lands.
Application code, the policy engine and rules.yaml. TRUSTED is never manufactured by validation and never by an approval: it comes only from configuration a person wrote.
Case is frozen and transition() is its only writer, so DONE is reachable only from VERIFYING. No graph edge leaves DONE; only an inbound event can.
OUTSIDE CARELOOP
Two external systems supported by the architecture; each is
verified by a separate read request.
Demo World clinic

g.text: demoworld/ — its own process, its own port. It may never
import careloop, which is what makes reading it back
evidence rather than the agent consulting itself.

svg.text: POST /clinic/appointments
the booking, under the idempotency key frozen before dispatch
GET /clinic/appointments/{confirmation_id}
a separate request, compared against what policy authorised
Amazon S3

g.text: No idempotency key and no notion of an action, so every
guarantee is assembled from create-once primitives. A 412
is settled by fetching and comparing the bytes.

svg.text: PutObject(IfNoneMatch="*")
upload_document, create-once under that same frozen identity
GetObject
a fresh read; the bytes are digested here, not taken on trust
The other two effects — send_email and grant_portal_access —
are simulated, and verification of those closes the loop on the
decision, not on the world.
CONTROLLED
what validation has earned the right to promote, and nothing more

g.text: Promoted UNTRUSTED to CONTROLLED by validation, and
only VALUE-class arguments are promotable at all.
DESTINATION and AUTHORITY never are, whatever a
Frozen. State, evidence, approvals, actions, and an
append-only timeline of what was proposed, what was
allowed or denied, which rule matched, and what
SQLite here, a DynamoDB-shaped interface. The durable
source of truth. Strands session persistence holds
execution context only and is never asked a business

svg.text: validated facts, with provenance
resolved trust is what the engine reads
DEPLOYED
CareLoop runs as one application process; Demo World runs as a second process on the same EC2 host.

Zone colours are claims about authority, not about code quality: UNTRUSTED means nothing here may decide anything, whoever wrote it.
